name: Red Hill
intro: On a misty basalt plateau above the Peninsula's central ridge, Red Hill has arranged some of the strongest food and wine in Victoria into a circuit that rewards the unhurried. A village by strict measure - a general store, a monthly market, vineyard restaurants that don't advertise from the highway - it nonetheless organises the whole upper Peninsula around itself. The winery restaurant cluster here - Ten Minutes by Tractor, Montalto, Paringa Estate, Principia - has no serious peer in the state. Come on Saturday; plan lunch first.
factualLede: Red Hill is the central hinterland village of the Mornington Peninsula's wine country, 85 km from Melbourne, on a cool-climate basalt plateau between Western Port and Port Phillip.

heroImage.alt: Pinot noir grapes ripening on the vine at Main Ridge Estate, Red Hill plateau

tldr: Red Hill is the Mornington Peninsula's wine and food epicentre - specifically Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, and orchards producing apples and cherries.
Best for: wine tourists, serious eaters, weekend stays that centre on food rather than beach.
Signature experience: cellar door Saturday followed by the Red Hill Market, then lunch at a vineyard restaurant.
Spend at least one full day; two nights if you're here for wine.
No beach within five minutes - that's not what Red Hill is for.
notFor: people trying to do the Peninsula cheaply
signature: The most concentrated food and wine precinct on the Peninsula, on the plateau above the bay.
skip: Trying to do more than three cellar doors in a day - the road between them is narrow and slow.
bestDay: Red Hill Market at 9am, producer trail through the morning, long lunch at one of the ridge restaurants, one cellar door in the afternoon.
insiderNote: The plateau is best early, before the market traffic and lunch bookings turn every short drive into a slow crawl.
